Subject: Quick question — ClearWave pilot: PO required?

Evelyn,

Quick context: ClearWave (Dana) is asking to start a three-week pilot next week. Scope is evaluation + 100k tokens of usage (estimated cost ~$2,750). They want a simple invoice after pilot rather than a formal PO.

I attached the vendor onboarding form they've started filling out. Procurement policy doc I saw says POs are required for vendor invoices over $5k/month. This pilot is below that threshold but legal/finance often push for a PO regardless.

Can procurement sign off on invoice-only for pilots under $5k? If not, what's the exception path/time to approve? Dana is sensitive to lead time — they want to kick off Monday.

Attaching: clearwave_vendor_onboarding_form.pdf

Next steps I propose:
- If procurement allows invoice-only: finance will route invoice and we proceed.
- If PO required: Ben to request PO from ClearWave and delay kickoff.

Thoughts?

Thanks,
Ben
--

Thanks for the background, Ben. Looping in finance and legal for a quick gate decision. A few clarifying items before I kick an exception through:

- Confirmed pilot total spend estimate: $2,750? Any chance it spikes above $5k during the 3 weeks?
- Has ClearWave provided W-9 / tax docs?
- Any data residency or SOC2 concerns flagged by security?

Jonas — can you weigh in on acceptable contractual coverage for a short pilot? Lauren — can finance approve an invoice-only route conditional on documentation?

If everyone agrees, I can approve a temporary invoice routing for the pilot only, with requirements captured in the exemption form.

Evelyn

On Mon, Mar 29, 2027 at 08:07 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jonas — can you weigh in on acceptable contractual coverage for a short pilot?

Short answer: we prefer a PO + MSA, but for short pilots under $10k we have an established exception path if we capture the scope and acceptance criteria in writing. Two options:

1) Fast route (preferred for sales velocity): Exception form + short email confirmation from vendor that they accept Redwood's standard ordering terms for the pilot and liability cap (I can draft the short acceptance language). Finance issues invoice-only routing for one-time pilot cost.

2) Conservative route: Request PO from vendor and execute MSA before kickoff.

Risks to surface: indemnity/PII, export controls, and refund/credit if pilot fails. If the vendor is a U.S. entity with SOC2 Type II attestation and W-9 on file, option 1 is reasonable.

Attaching: exemption-request-form.pdf (fillable) — please complete and route to procurement for my review.

Jonas
--
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question — ClearWave pilot: PO required?

Thanks for the context. Finance position: we can approve an invoice-only pathway for a one-time pilot capped at $6,000 provided all of the following conditions are met BEFORE revenue recognition:

- Completed vendor onboarding form on file (we have the draft Ben attached).
- W-9 and tax paperwork uploaded to vendor profile.
- SOC2 Type II summary reviewed (no red flags).
- Signed one-page confirmation of scope and acceptance (I agree Jonas can draft this).

If those are satisfied, procurement can sign the exemption and finance will route the invoice without a PO for this pilot only. This approval is strictly for the single pilot and does not establish recurring non-PO billing.

Please action:
- Ben: get W-9 + confirm SOC2 attestation link from ClearWave.
- Jonas: send short acceptance language and I will attach to the exemption.
- Evelyn: once exemption signed, route to accounting@redwood.com for payment setup.

Attaches: clearwave-soc2-summary.pdf

Lauren Bishop
Director, Finance Operations
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
